findings.title: select().all() returns tuples not scalars
findings.problem: Line 497-499 executes select(Budget.budget_id).all() which returns a list of Row tuples [(id,), (id,), ...]. Line 500 converts to strings but still operates on tuples. Line 502 uses .in_(soft_deleted_budgets) which receives tuples instead of scalar ids.
findings.impact: The UPDATE query fails or matches no rows because .in_() receives [(id,)] instead of [id]. Soft-deleted budgets are not unlinked from the project, and the foreign key constraint violation persists, blocking project deletion.

findings.title: join lacks created_at tie-breaker for deterministic row selection
findings.problem: Lines 252-259 join on user_identifier, budget_category, spend_date, and created_at from the subquery that groups by max(created_at). However, if multiple ProjectSpendTracking rows share the same spend_date and created_at (created within same millisecond), the join picks an arbitrary row among them.
findings.impact: Admin user list shows wrong spending value when multiple spend snapshots exist for the same date and created_at. The query is non-deterministic.
findings.recommendation: Add ProjectSpendTracking.id DESC as tie-breaker in the subquery aggregation and join condition to ensure deterministic row selection.

findings.title: 4 commits use non-ticket format
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires EPMCDME-####: Description format for all commits. 4 commits in this branch use task-slug prefix format (fix-project-deletion-fk-violation: ..., budget-assignment-record-spending: ...) instead of the required EPMCDME-####: format.
findings.impact: Commit format convention ensures traceability to Jira work items and consistent git history navigation. Non-compliant commits break tooling that parses commit messages for ticket extraction.
findings.recommendation: Rebase or squash-merge to a single commit with EPMCDME-13156: format before final review completion.
